name: CR-Int-13-parts-2.c
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
If \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) -
 F(b).\]

So, we need to calculate \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}.\]

By linearity, \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:4}} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}}\]

So, using integration by parts, that is if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of {{CT:6}} then \[\int u dv = uv - \int v du,\] by defining \(u = {{CT:7}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that

\(du = {{CT:9}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:10}}\).

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:7}}\left[{{CT:10}}\right] - \int \left[{{CT:10}}\right]{{CT:9}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}} - \int {{CT:12}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}}
 \end{array}\]

Hence, \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:14}} = {{CT:15}}\]

Let \(F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:15}}\)

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:16}} - {{CT:17}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number.  This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
